summary: a declared lane never wakes the inbox slice, so a quiet tree hibernates over a red lane — and with no closing condition a woken lane would re-drain the same run every tick

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: the inbox slice is live for a declared lane exactly when that lane's latest completed run for the tip's branch failed and is past the lane's stamp; a green run, an already-stamped run, and a lane it cannot read each make it live for nothing.
tests: the inbox slice is live when a declared lane's latest completed run failed past the lane's stamp
the inbox slice is not live when the lane's failing run is the one already stamped
the inbox slice is not live when the lane's latest completed run passed
the inbox slice is not live when the forge CLI cannot read the lane
notes: `PlanSliceWindow.live` is sync and runs on the selection path (planState.ts), so the lane read has a sync half — once per tick per lane, beside the render's. `SliceInputs` carries no working tree, so the liveness leg must read the branch at the same repo root the render does (`ci.ts`, *The branch is the repo's*) or the two readers name different runs. The agent writes the stamp as it writes a cursor, so the rendered block must name the run it would stamp.

per.section: CI lanes as a findings source

acceptance: a failing lane's rendered log carries no forge decoration on any line, and a line the forge framed around nothing costs no budget; the drain reads failing titles from the head of the log rather than trimming them away.
tests: the shed strips the forge's frame from a log line the job name frames without a timestamp
the shed drops a log line the forge framed around an empty message
notes: Lane-observed on run 35008214078: ~380 tail lines rendered as `windows\tRun pnpm test\t…`, many holding nothing but the prefix, while 1160 head lines — carrying three reds' titles — were trimmed. The job name is a fact the lane declared (`CiLane.job`), so the frame is read, not guessed (`engine-boundary.md`, *Told, not inferred*); a bare two-field strip would eat the leading columns of any tab-carrying test output.

edit.description: `plantForge` puts the stub's dir on a PATH the host's own forge CLI is not on, so the direct spawn reaches the stub or nothing

summary: `plantForge` prepends its dir but leaves the host's PATH behind it, so on a host whose real `gh` the direct spawn can reach, five cases read the forge instead of the stub
acceptance: every lane-reader case is answered by the planted stub on every host, and the vacuity pins on the stub's call count hold for the stub's own invocations rather than for a CLI the fixture never planted.
pins: every lane-reader case reads its planted forge stub, with the host's own forge CLI off PATH
notes: Lane-observed: the `refuses` case rendered the real `gh`'s GH_TOKEN message, and the other four saw `calls().length === 0`. On win32 the stub is a `.cmd`, which a direct spawn skips; the search then walks on to the host's `gh.exe` further down PATH. The helper's own doc comment already states the isolation this breaks, and the absent-CLI case already shows the shape — PATH stripped to a single dir, the launcher naming `process.execPath` absolutely.

edit.description: the silent arm takes absence from the path, not from an errno that means two things
the obstructed-root case, asserted on the refusal rather than on a platform's errno

summary: readAll reads `ENOENT` from the keyspace readdir as nothing-written, and on win32 a plain file at the prior-attempts root raises exactly that — an unreachable store reports as no records
acceptance: an obstructed prior-attempts root refuses on every supported host, and only a genuinely absent path reads as no records.
pins: readAll refuses when a plain file sits at the prior-attempts root
notes: Lane-observed twice: `readAll refuses when the prior-attempts dir is present but unreadable` resolved `Map{}` on windows-latest where POSIX raises ENOTDIR. The doc comment on readAll already names this exact degradation as the one it refuses to make. No `tests[]`: the errno split is unreproducible on a POSIX base, so the windows lane's own title is the verification (`spec/cli.md`, *win32 is a supported host*). Sibling ENOENT-means-absent arms in src/job.ts are not yet lane-evidenced.
